newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks close up on IMF hopes, liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks close up on IMF hopes, liquidity.

text.p: Thai stocks closed higher in thin trade on Monday on high liquidity and as investors bought on hopes that the government would accept an economic package proposed by the IMF, brokers said.

"The market closed higher as expected earlier. Investors anticipated that the government would accept the economic package which could help the country's ailing economy. High liquidity in the money market was another factor boosting the sentiment," said Songyos Kulvichien of Securities One.
The composite SET index closed 11.78 points higher at 663.82 on 3.4 billion baht turnover.

Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya told reporters earlier in the day that discussions were still going on with the IMF but the basic framework of a package would be presented and was expected to be approved by cabinet on Tuesday.

Bank of Thailand Governor Chaiyawat Wibulswasdi said the package could be painful but the government would try to ease its impact. He did not say how the government would minimise the impact of the austerity measures.
Brokers said high liquidity in the money market due to sales of the U.S. unit by exporters helped boost market sentiment.
Exporters sold the U.S. dollar as they also anticipated positive results for the baht from an acceptance of IMF measures.

Most of the key sectors advanced except the property sector, which dipped 0.93 percent. The finance sector rose most in terms of value, gaining 2.66 percent. Nava Finance topped the active list in terms of value, rising 2.25 baht to 32.50.
Brokers said they expected the market to continue rising on Tuesday on buying ahead of the announcement on the IMF rescue package. -- Suthep Chawla (662) 652-0642, email: bangkok.newsroom@reuters.com
